newsitem.title: UK: IGC sees higher world coarse grain crop, stocks.
newsitem.headline: IGC sees higher world coarse grain crop, stocks.

text.p: The International Grains Council (IGC) forecast world coarse grain production to reach 869 million tonnes in 1996, 3.0 million tonnes higher than its previous estimate, the IGC said on Thursday.
The projected increase was mainly due to a higher forecast for the European Union (EU), whose output was pegged at 148.8 million tonnes, 2.6 million up on the IGC's August forecast.
A record maize crop was expected in Spain and the British barley crop was forecast to improve considerably, the IGC said.
The IGC raised its estimate for world coarse grain stocks by 7.0 million tonnes to 100 million tonnes, with the main increases expected in the U.S. and European Union (EU).

U.S. stocks were projected at 22 million tonnes and EU barley carryover stocks could increase from 7.0 million tonnes, with 2.0 million in intervention, in 1996 to nearly 10.0 million in 1997, the IGC said.
The higher production figure was offset by an estimated fall in Russian output, although the U.S. forecast was also higher.
Russia would produce 39.0 million tonnes of coarse grains in 1996, the IGC said, 2.0 million tonnes less than its August forecast.
While Russian barley yields are reported to be down in some areas, reducing the IGC estimate, final output will still be higher than last year.
The forecast for U.S. production was raised by 1.0 million tonnes to 255.6 million, with better prospects for maize yields seen in Illinois, Iowa and Nebraska.
World trade in coarse grains for 1996 was projected slightly lower at 89 million tonnes, 2.0 million under the earlier projection, due largely to a lower figure for maize purchases by China.
China was expected to import 2.2 million tonnes of coarse grains in 1996/97, compared with the IGC's earlier estimate of 3.6 million and 1995/96 imports totalling 5.1 million.
